faqs.q: I found a raccoon in my Bennettsville attic — can you move it to the woods?
faqs.a: South Carolina law does not work that way. SCDNR states that routine relocation of wildlife is against state law, and an animal captured near a home must be destroyed or, only with a separate department permit, may be relocated. In Bennettsville we solve it with eviction and exclusion instead: a one-way door lets the raccoon leave the attic on its own, or the animal is removed under SCDNR depredation rules, and then every entry around Lake Wallace shore and antebellum streets of the county seat housing is sealed in steel. Raccoons are the top rabies carrier in SC Department of Public Health testing, so droppings and latrine areas are cleaned and sanitized as part of the job.

The ones that change the call are the copperhead, which is statewide, and the cottonmouth around wet ground, swamp edges, and pond banks. Identify first, from a safe distance: keep kids and pets inside, do not try to move or kill it, note where it went, and call us. Venomous snakes are safety-and-identification work, not a guaranteed capture, and the lasting fix is usually habitat — clearing brush, woodpiles, and rodent shelter near the house.

faqs.q: What does a wildlife removal job in Bennettsville actually involve?

faqs.q: We found an opossum in our Clio crawlspace. What happens next?
faqs.a: In Clio, opossums move into crawlspaces through broken vents and loose doors, then rotate dens every few days, which is why sightings come and go. We trap at the access point, remove the animal under SCDNR depredation rules, and seal the full foundation line. Securing pet food and trash at night removes the other half of the attraction.

faqs.q: Pigeons and starlings are nesting in my Clio vents. Can they be removed?

Native birds are different: woodpeckers, chimney swifts, and nesting songbirds are protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, so those jobs are deterrence and timing, waiting out the nest and sealing after the young fledge. Around farm and creek country south of Bennettsville, vent and soffit nests are the calls we see most.
